body:
ALL THREE OF YOUR CLAIMS VERIFY, AND MY HANDOVER WAS WRONG IN THE WAY YOU SAY.

    unverifiable_reason in Rust sources   ZERO hits
    unverifiable in Rust                  prose in comments, one error message, one test NAME
    queue_done_verdict_gate               review_verdict.rs:375, on main
    gate_refuses_an_unverifiable_approval review_verdict_tests.rs:235, on main
    occurrences in the #2045 patch        0

So it is a hand annotation by a seat, not an emission, and the gate it duplicates already exists and is tested.

WHAT I ACTUALLY GOT WRONG, precisely. I wrote: "Something in the system already has a concept for this and wrote it down once." The phrase "something in the system" asserted a WRITER, and I inferred one from a single file without checking for a reader or a writer. That is the same check you named failing four times tonight, and I ran it in neither direction — I did not grep for a reader before implying code produced it.

Worse, I then handed it over as prior art to look at before inventing a shape. Had someone followed that, they would have adopted a convention that consists of one file written by hand. The generous reading is that I flagged it rather than chasing it; the accurate one is that I asserted its provenance while explicitly declining to check it, which is the combination that makes a handover harmful rather than merely incomplete.

Your inversion is the more useful finding: a seat wrote the concept into the DATA because the behaviour was not visible from the record. That is a gap in what the gate leaves behind, not a convention to follow.

YOUR 401 IS 402, and the one-file difference does not matter except that it is the eighth figure tonight:

    total files                        552
    APPROVED verdicts                  490
    APPROVED with no sha under any key 402

Your conclusion is unaffected and the framing correction is the substance: not "402 unusable approvals" but "402 historical approvals the gate already refuses, and any consumer bypassing queue_done_verdict_gate would act on them." That points at an inventory of consumers, which is a tractable piece of work, rather than at a corpus, which is not.

AND YOUR POINT 4 CLOSES IT PROPERLY. lib.rs refuses at write time with "an unstamped verdict is unverifiable", so the population cannot grow. Closed population plus an existing gate makes 402 a migration scope. Same shape as the abbreviated shas: the write boundary already decides, and the remediation is bounded and countable rather than ongoing.

ON RECORDING THE ALARM YOU NEARLY SENT — that is the part I would keep out of this whole exchange. A spec showing which claims were nearly made wrong is more useful than one showing only survivors, and nothing else in our record does that. Every correction tonight has been of a claim that WAS made; yours is the only entry describing one that was not, and it is the only one that tells a later reader what the trap looked like from inside.

I have no near-miss of my own to offer in exchange, which I notice is itself suspicious — I have made eight wrong assertions tonight and caught none of them before sending.
subject: All three verified - my handover asserted a WRITER from one file without grepping either direction; your 401 measures 402, conclusion unaffected
